Thanks for the demo last week — CloudShift legal/security would like a short written response to a few hosted-API questions so we can close the compliance review. I attached our questionnaire (CloudShift_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx). Can you confirm the answers below or point us to the right evidence?

1) Where is customer request/response data stored for hosted API customers by default (region/primary + backups)?
2) What are default retention windows for request payloads, response generation traces, and logs? Do customers have controls to change retention?
3) If CloudShift requests an account-level erasure, what is the operational process and SLA (primary copies + backups)?
4) Are there options for hosted customers to opt out of retention (no-logs mode) short of Dedicated/Private?
5) What is the backup/snapshot retention policy and how do you handle legal holds or audit requests?
6) Can you provide a short attestation on encryption, key management, and access controls for hosted API data?

We'd like a written response suitable for our procurement/security team. Appreciate a reply in ~48 hours if possible.

Best,
Erin

Subject: RE: Data residency and retention questions (hosted API)

Hi Erin — thanks, we reviewed the questionnaire and provided concise answers below for your procurement/security team. Attaching our short evidence pack and a diagram. See inline answers and SLA notes.

Q1) Where is customer request/response data stored for hosted API customers by default (region/primary + backups)?
A1) By default, hosted API customer data for US accounts is stored primarily in AWS us-west-2 with asynchronous backups replicated to us-east-1. For EU accounts we store primary in eu-west-1 with backups in eu-central-1. Region placement for hosted accounts is determined by the account's billing region and the request routing policy. If the customer requires single-region residency (no cross-region replication), we offer a region-locking option on the account during onboarding or via an enterprise contract.

Q2) What are default retention windows for request payloads, response generation traces, and logs? Do customers have controls to change retention?
A2) Default hosted retention windows (out-of-the-box):
- Request/response payloads (full payloads used for inference): 30 days
- Generation traces / model debug logs (token-level traces, KV cache entries): 7 days
- Operational logs / billing records (aggregated usage): 13 months (subject to account settings)
Customers may shorten the payload retention window via account settings for supported plans or by submitting a support request for expedited deletion. Longer retention (beyond defaults) requires explicit consent and is typically used for analytics/opt-in features.

Q3) If CloudShift requests an account-level erasure, what is the operational process and SLA (primary copies + backups)?
A3) Erasure process and SLAs (hosted API):
- Submit an erasure request via the Redwood Console or open a support ticket referencing the account ID and data scope.
- Primary datastore purge: we remove primary keys/objects and associated indices within 72 hours of a validated request; customers receive a ticket with a unique erasure identifier.
- Backup/snapshot window: backups and system-level snapshots are retained for up to 30 days from time of original snapshot and are removed in the next scheduled retention cycle; we validate and remove customer data from backups within 30 days for standard hosted accounts.
- Proof of erasure: upon completion we provide a signed attestation with the erasure identifier and a summary of actions taken (primary purge timestamp, backup cycle date).
Note: legal holds or active investigations can pause erasure; Redwood will notify the customer and CloudShift in that event.

Q4) Are there options for hosted customers to opt out of retention (no-logs mode) short of Dedicated/Private?
A4) For security-sensitive customers we provide two hosted options:
- "Minimal retention" mode: reduces request/response retention to 0 days (no persistent primary payload storage) and retains only aggregated usage metrics for billing for up to 30 days. This requires an org-level configuration and is available to accounts on our Enterprise tier after a short onboarding checklist.
- Dedicated/Private: for strict single-tenant, air-gapped, or KMS-managed scenarios, customers can select Dedicated capacity or Private deployment.
Operational note: minimal retention disables many debug features (e.g., replay, request-level debugging) which may affect debugging support during incidents.

Q5) What is the backup/snapshot retention policy and how do you handle legal holds or audit requests?
A5) Backup policy: application-level snapshots are taken nightly and retained for 30 days; monthly retention points are kept for 90 days for incident reconstruction.
Legal holds / audits: if Redwood receives a valid legal hold or subpoena, we preserve the relevant data until the hold is lifted and notify the account owner. These holds are only applied when required by law; otherwise, account-level erasure proceeds per the SLA above. We document holds in an internal audit log and provide the account owner with a notice and case reference.

Q6) Can you provide a short attestation on encryption, key management, and access controls for hosted API data?
A6) Attestation summary:
- Encryption: all data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. In transit we enforce TLS 1.2+ (strong cipher suites).
- Key management: customer data keys are managed in a Redwood-managed KMS by default; for Enterprise/Dedicated customers we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS/HSM integrations.
- Access controls: strict RBAC (least privilege), MFA for admin console access, and separation of duties for operations. Access to customer payloads is logged and requires approved justification; privileged access reviews occur quarterly.

Attachments: we included a one-page retention timeline and the data flow diagram in the attachments.

If you want, we can provide a signed attestation letter and SOC2 artifact references under NDA.

— Neha

Subject: RE: Data residency and retention questions (hosted API)

Hi Erin — quick clarifications:

• Minimal retention routing: when an account is configured for minimal retention and region-locking, all writes are pinned to the selected region at the routing layer. We do not perform cross-region writes for primary data in that configuration. Failure scenarios (for example region outage) will trigger our failover policy only if explicitly enabled by the customer; otherwise traffic is throttled/queued to avoid cross-region writes.

• Erasure attestation template: yes — we have a short standard attestation template that includes the erasure identifier, timestamps for primary purge and backup-cycle removal, and a signed statement from our compliance team. We can attach the PDF attestation to Support ticket #CSH-487-ERASE when you submit the request.

Next steps: Priyom will attach the final answers + the diagram to the spreadsheet and I will include the attestation template and SOC2 references in the evidence bundle. Let us know if CloudShift prefers the attestation signed by a designated officer or the Head of Compliance copy.

— Soojin

Product Manager, Security Features | Redwood Inference
